clue.text: Left in second year, preferring to play

indicators.note: in says the word for left sits inside the two abbreviations

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A student kept back a year who would rather be off playing than studying.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sporty is keen on games and would rather be playing them.

clue.text: Friends upset, then cheerful, taking things as they come?

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned over, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: pals are friends
happy means cheerful

explanation.surface: Friends fall out, then cheer up, accepting whatever happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns PALS into SLAP; 'then' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone slaphappy is casually careless, accepting events without worry.

clue.text: Endless rage after some deliveries took too long

indicators.note: after puts the trimmed rage word behind the deliveries word

parts.note: an over in cricket is a set of six deliveries

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to rant is to rage

explanation.surface: Someone fumes endlessly after parcels arrive late.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an OVER is six balls bowled by one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun is to exceed the allotted time, so overran means took too long.

clue.text: US lawyer's engaged in trifling item now

indicators.note: engaged in means the lawyer abbreviation is set inside the trinket word

parts.note: a toy is a trifle, something of little value
DA is a district attorney, an American prosecutor

explanation.surface: An American attorney is currently busy with some trivial matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Today can mean nowadays, at the present time.

clue.text: Business intent on reproducing success

parts.note: read literally, a business whose aim is to breed more winners, horses bred from champion sires

explanation.surface: A company determined to repeat its earlier triumphs.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests corporate strategy; 'reproducing' is meant literally, as breeding, and the 'success' is a winning racehorse put out to stud.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud establishment breeds horses, aiming to produce foals from successful racing stock.

clue.text: Discussion of Satanism required? Here's the very fellow!

definitions.meaning: said when the person just mentioned walks in

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom greets someone who appears just as they are mentioned; literally it is chat about Satan.

clue.text: Cashier finally resigning during record run

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: during puts the final letter inside the run word

parts.note: to hare is to run fast

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of resigning

explanation.surface: A bank cashier quits halfway through a recording session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cashier' looks like the bank clerk but is the verb, to dismiss from service.
explanation.definitionFit: To cashier an officer is to dismiss them from the armed forces, to discharge them.

clue.text: Star soldier -a personification of war

parts.note: a soldier ant is a kind of ant
Ares is the Greek god of war

explanation.surface: A celebrated soldier described as war incarnate.
explanation.definitionFit: Antares is the bright red star in the constellation Scorpius.

clue.text: Foremost of ministers in Church getting chop

indicators.note: foremost of picks the opening letter of ministers

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The leading minister in the Church faces the axe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' links; 'chop' is the verb, to cut finely.
explanation.definitionFit: To mince meat is to chop it very finely.

clue.text: Industrial action value for money, leading to deal?

parts.note: a strike is industrial action by workers
a bargain is good value for money

explanation.surface: Strikers win a good deal from management in a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading to' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike a bargain is to agree terms, to make a deal.

clue.text: Version of tale can do as a story

indicators.note: a version of something is a reworking of it, so the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A retelling of a tale may serve as a story.
explanation.definitionFit: Anecdotal evidence comes from stories people tell rather than from systematic study.

clue.text: Material's almost cloying

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: sating means filling to excess, cloying

explanation.surface: A fabric described as almost too rich, sickly sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Material stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a smooth glossy fabric, a kind of material.

clue.text: Novelist making way through grass?

indicators.note: through puts the way abbreviation running inside the word for grass

parts.note: hay is dried grass
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A writer cutting a path through a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas HARDY wrote Tess of the d'Urbervilles.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hardy was an English novelist of rural Wessex life.

clue.text: Heroin supplied by club? People made tracks for this!

indicators.note: supplied by places the word for the drug after the word for club, its supplier

parts.note: an iron is a golf club
horse is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A club where drugs are dealt, and people leave in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made tracks' sounds like fleeing, but the tracks are railway lines laid for the locomotive.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron horse is an old nickname for a steam locomotive, which runs on laid railway tracks.

clue.text: Car repairer who did well on What's My Line?

definitions.meaning: a tradesman who hammers out dents in car bodywork

definitions.text: who did well on What's My Line?
definitions.meaning: a guest on the TV quiz whose job the celebrity panel failed to guess, so they beat the panel

explanation.walkthrough: What's My Line? was a TV game show in which a panel tried to guess a contestant's occupation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who knocks out dents is one sense; a contestant who beat the panel is the other.

clue.text: Granted, Wagner's operas will have no opening for happy characters

parts.note: let means allowed, granted

indicators.note: will have no means a letter is taken away from the operas phrase

parts.note: The Ring is Wagner's cycle of four operas

indicators.note: opening for picks the first letter of happy

explanation.surface: Admittedly, Wagner's operas offer nothing to cheerful types.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will have no' takes H from THE RING, leaving TERING; 'characters' means letters, not people.
explanation.definitionFit: Lettering is the set of written characters on a sign or page.

clue.text: It's recalled as a command to a dog

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the word is turned around

parts.note: 'tis is the old contraction of it is

explanation.surface: A phrase remembered as an order to a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: Owners tell a dog to sit when they want it to settle on its haunches.

clue.text: Scripture examination, in which uninspired note is penned

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, so the dull note is shut inside the exam word

parts.note: a test is an examination
tame means dull, uninspired

explanation.surface: A Bible exam in which a dull remark gets written down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' suggests writing but means shut in a pen; 'in which' links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old and New Testaments are the two parts of Christian scripture.

clue.text: Certainly watches leader being deposed

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: eyes as a verb means watches

explanation.surface: A political observer is sure the leader is about to fall.
explanation.definitionFit: An affirmative reply, agreeing that something is certainly so.

clue.text: Malicious gossip in South Carolina and Alabama

parts.note: SC is the postal abbreviation for South Carolina
AL is the postal abbreviation for Alabama

explanation.surface: Spiteful rumours circulating in two southern states.
explanation.definitionFit: Scandal is talk spreading rumours that damage reputations.

clue.text: A way of taking court activity on board?

definitions.text: A way of taking court activity on board?

parts.words: A way of taking court activity on board?
parts.note: read literally, a court game such as tennis moved onto a board, a tabletop

explanation.surface: Bringing a legal process aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests law and 'on board' a ship; it is a tennis court and a table.
explanation.definitionFit: Ping-pong is a version of a racket game played on a table instead of a court.

clue.text: No bridge team will get first place continuously

parts.note: North and South are partners in bridge, a team
top is first place

explanation.surface: A card team that will never come first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will get' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-stop means without pause, continuously.

clue.text: Where university course may lead, though not entirely

definitions.meaning: studies at university lead towards an academic qualification

explanation.walkthrough: 'though' links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase is heading for a qualification; idiomatically it means to some extent.

clue.text: Deliberately lose most of the argument

indicators.note: most of means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a row is an argument

explanation.surface: Concede most of a quarrel on purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw a game is to lose it on purpose.

clue.text: The present chap is a soldier in South Africa

indicators.note: in puts the soldier inside the country's abbreviation

parts.note: a soldier ant is a kind of ant, so ant stands for soldier

explanation.surface: A man stationed with the army in South Africa right now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' reads as 'current' but means gift; 'is a' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Christmas is the figure who brings children their gifts.

clue.text: Start a fight

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb phrase it means begin in earnest; as a noun, a scuffle or bout.

clue.text: More than one spoke, with transmitter cutting off last one

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a radio transmits signals
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Several people spoke, and a broadcaster cut off the final speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoke' looks like a verb but is the noun, a wheel spoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Radii is the plural of radius, and a radius is a spoke of a wheel.

clue.text: Realist unsettled, but holding to philosopher

indicators.note: holding means the rearranged letters wrap round the short word
unsettled letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A realist, disturbed, still clings to a great thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a realist shaken but clinging to Aristotle; 'but' is a link word joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle was the ancient Greek philosopher, pupil of Plato.

clue.text: Some German group going behind gorge

indicators.note: going behind puts the group word after the gorge word

parts.note: to wolf is to gorge, to eat greedily
a gang is a group

explanation.surface: A band of Germans trekking behind a ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gorge' looks like a ravine but is the verb to eat greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfgang is a German given name, as in Mozart, so it names one German.

clue.text: Stolen drug seen in dish

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Stolen narcotics found in a serving bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancashire HOTPOT is a British stew of meat topped with sliced potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotpot is a slow-cooked stew, a dish of meat and vegetables.
